Here's an example of how to sort an array of objects by a numeric field called `count` using JavaScript:

```javascript
// Example array of objects with a 'count' property
const items = [
  { name: 'Item A', count: 17 },
  { name: 'Item B', count: 24 },
  { name: 'Item C', count: 30 }
];

// Sort the array by the 'count' field in ascending order
items.sort((a, b) => a.count - b.count);

// Output the sorted array
console.log('Sorted items:', items);
```

**Output:**
```
Sorted items: [
  { name: 'Item A', count: 17 },
  { name: 'Item B', count: 24 },
  { name: 'Item C', count: 30 }
]
```

### Sorting in Descending Order

To sort in descending order (highest to lowest), reverse the comparison:

```javascript
items.sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count);
```
